title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
slides: Why did Spotify purge 50 million tracks now?
The platform acted to clean its recommendation algorithm
Most spam tracks came from AI-generated music factories
Your Discover Weekly may sound different this week
Check your playlist: fewer tracks, better signal
thread_text:
1. Spotify's silent purge

50 million tracks just vanished overnight. The company says it's about cleaning up recommendations, not saving storage.

2. The algorithm's diet

Spotify's recommendation engine was drowning in noise. The platform cut the junk to make your Discover Weekly sharper.

3. AI music factories exposed

Most of the deleted tracks came from automated music farms. They were gaming the system with thousands of fake artists.

4. Your playlist is changing

Fewer tracks means less variety in some genres. But the signal-to-noise ratio should improve for your daily mixes.

5. Check your Discover Weekly

Open the app and see if your recommendations feel different. Then ask: did this purge actually help your listening?

instagram.caption:
50 million tracks just disappeared from Spotify's recommendations — almost all of them AI-generated music from automated factories churning out fake artists 🎧

The platform pulled them to clean its recommendation algorithm, which was drowning in noise. Less junk in the system means your Discover Weekly and daily mixes should get sharper.

If you make music, this raises the bar: mass-produced tracks gaming the algorithm are now being cut, so real signal matters more than volume.

Open your Discover Weekly this week — does it sound different to you? 👀
